derivation_notes: The parent already applies a multiplicative contraction/separation loss but still assumes the accelerating core follows an isentropic branch shape. Here an added loading- and temperature-dependent entropy-production surrogate reduces the effective subcritical expansion exponent, producing a polytropic-like branch with altered curvature while leaving the choked asymptote branch unchanged.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption of purely isentropic subcritical expansion by introducing a pressure-drop- and temperature-dependent reduction of the effective expansion exponent. This changes the unchoked m_dot versus r_p curvature instead of only rescaling the curve.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Subcritical compressible expansion through the effective restriction is isentropic apart from a multiplicative discharge-loss prefactor.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Pressure-drop-driven entropy generation and nonuniform contraction make the effective expansion through the restriction polytropic rather than strictly isentropic, altering the subcritical pressure-ratio dependence before full choking is reached.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting poly_entropy_coeff = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed A, p0, and gas constants, the pressure-ratio response is set by one smooth subcritical isentropic branch multiplied by a monotone loss factor, then capped by a choked plateau; temperature only shifts this through the effective gamma and loss magnitude.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same subcritical-to-choked structure but replace the purely isentropic pressure-ratio dependence with a real-gas polytropic/entropy-producing expansion surrogate whose exponent varies with loading, so the subcritical m_dot(r_p) curvature and approach to the limiting regime change systematically with pressure drop and temperature.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed A and p0, two temperatures can show different bending of m_dot versus r_p in the unchoked regime, not just a shifted level or threshold; the child allows earlier flattening of the curve as pressure drop grows, while still matching the same choked asymptote constraint.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: With A and p0 held fixed, sweep r_p through the subcritical regime at two T0 values. The parent predicts one isentropic branch family times a separable loss prefactor, so temperature mainly shifts level and the choke point. The child predicts a genuine change in branch bending: at higher T0 and appreciable 1 - r_p, m_dot flattens earlier as r_p decreases toward the limiting regime, while the choked branch remains on the same asymptotic form.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because its subcritical dependence is structurally constrained to an isentropic branch determined by gamma_eff(T0), then multiplied by a separable loss factor. Refitting gamma_drop_max, T_gamma_scale, loss_coeff, loss_exponent, and loss_temp_exponent can move level and threshold and reshape curves only within that fixed branch family, but cannot create loading-dependent, temperature-dependent curvature changes inside the pressure-ratio exponents while simultaneously preserving the same choked asymptote with one shared fit.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable for moderate to strong pressure drops below but near the limiting regime, especially when 1 - r_p is appreciable and T0 is high enough that boundary-layer growth and entropy production are not negligible, yet flow remains within the steady adiabatic restriction scenario.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as non-self-similar subcritical m_dot(r_p) curvature across T0; in holdout, the same effect extends toward lower r_p where the approach to the plateau differs from any single shared isentropic-shape parent fit.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of vanishing additional entropy production so the effective expansion exponent returns to the parent gamma_eff and the original branch shape is restored.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model already includes losses as an external multiplicative discharge penalty and a shifted choke boundary, but it still assumes the surviving accelerating core follows an isentropic pressure-ratio shape within each branch.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the parent assumption that subcritical compressible expansion through the effective restriction is isentropic apart from a prefactor loss; allow irreversible contraction/separation to modify the expansion exponent itself.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Pressure-drop-driven entropy generation and nonuniform contraction make the effective expansion through the restriction polytropic rather than strictly isentropic, altering the subcritical pressure-ratio dependence before full choking is reached.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with A, p0 fixed, m_dot rises as r_p decreases according to one ideal compressible branch shape based on gamma_eff(T0), merely scaled down by the loss factor and then switched to a capped branch. Child change: under the same fixed A and p0, vary r_p across the subcritical regime at two distinct T0 values. The proposed refinement changes the slope and curvature of m_dot versus r_p itself, because irreversible contraction/separation affects not only the overall discharge level but also how pressure energy is converted to acceleration as loading grows. Observable contrast: near but above the limiting pressure ratio, the child predicts stronger flattening of m_dot(r_p) with decreasing r_p at high T0 than at low T0, beyond what the parent can generate by one shared refit of gamma-drop and multiplicative loss parameters, since those preserve a single isentropic branch family times a separable prefactor. Admissible activation requires meaningful pressure drop and non-negligible irreversible structure while remaining in steady one-dimensional benchmark conditions. Limitation: if experiments only sample very weak pressure drops or only fully choked points, this refinement would be hard to distinguish.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Introduce a gain or loss that competes with an existing process in different state regions.

scenario_text: A compressible gas passes steadily through a converging restriction from a reservoir into a lower-pressure region. The benchmark predicts mass flow rate from the reservoir pressure, reservoir temperature, restriction area, and downstream-to-upstream pressure ratio. Compressible acceleration initially makes the flow sensitive to downstream pressure, but beyond a limiting condition the restriction cannot transmit further downstream influence upstream. The response is derived from steady compressible mass and momentum transport through the restriction.
